newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Turnover soars, Nigerian shares higher.
newsitem.headline: Turnover soars, Nigerian shares higher.

text.p: Nigerian stock trading continued its ascent on Wednesday, boosted by big price gains and increased turnover, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 6338.00 from 6296.25 on Tuesday and volume traded shot up to 2,590,215 from 639,643.
A single transaction for one million shares of Nigerian Wire Industry was executed, putting the building materials sector ahead of others.

Some 400,000 shares of Benue Cement Company in the same sector changed hands at 4.25 naira, 20 kobo higher than Tuesday's close, while West African Portland Cement was 20 kobo higher at 30.50 and Ashaka Cement five kobo up at 15.80 naira.
But the biggest rise was by oil marketer Unipetrol which added 70 kobo to 37.00 naira.
PZ Industries was also among gainers, closing at 34.70 naira, up 25 kobo, while Lever Brothers advanced 17 kobo to 25.37 naira.
Food shares also rose. Cadbury was 13 kobo higher at 24.53 naira, and Flour Mills went 10 kobo up at 9.70 naira, the same as Union Dicon Salt which closed at 32.76 naira.
The sector's biggest gainer was Coca-Cola bottler Nigerian Bottling Company, rising 25 kobo to 27.25 naira.
NAL Merchant Bank, however, slumped by 10 kobo to 5.50 naira and Afribank, which listed a fresh 100 million shares on Wednesday, also fell by 10 kobo to 5.50 naira.
CFAO remained under pressure, falling by six kobo to 4.69 naira. Seven-Up Bottling Company too was five down at 1.70 naira due to excess supply in the market.
Poor trading outlook continued to adversely affect packaging firms, forcing Avon Crowncaps down three kobo to 4.55 naira and CMB by five kobo to 4.30 naira.
